category_title: Students who work ahead and disrupt lessons with frequent procedural questions
minimal_context: The student is working ahead independently in a self-contained unit workbook while the teacher leads a group discussion on the board.
dialogue:
TUTOR: You can continue working ahead independently in your unit workbook while I record the joint working on the board for the rest of the group.

STUDENT: Excuse me Miss . . . do I need to copy the problems down or just write the answers?

TUTOR: Just do what you think is right.

STUDENT: Excuse me Miss . . . I'm on the next page now, what am I supposed to do for this section?

TUTOR: Please keep trying to work through it.

STUDENT: Excuse me Miss . . . I'm working ahead at a faster pace and I need you to tell me the procedure for the next unit.

options.A: Talk with the student's parents about their progress and frequently mention this possibility during class.
options.B: Have the student use a digital app to take notes, organize their workbook pages, and archive past units.
options.C: Schedule more time for the independent workbook sessions, extending them to 30 minutes rather than 15.
options.D: Explicitly incorporate instructional elements into the independent unit workbooks that promote student self-compassion during class.
